replayr

Pure-R parsers for 12 emulator movie (“input log”) file formats used by the speedrun and tool-assisted-speedrun communities.

Format Emulator Platforms
.fm2 FCEUX NES
.bk2 BizHawk (multi-system) NES, SNES, Genesis, Master System, GB/GBC/GBA, N64, PSX, Saturn, Atari 2600, PC Engine, Intellivision, ColecoVision, Arcade
.fcm FCEU NES
.lsmv lsnes SNES, Game Boy, Super Game Boy
.gmv Gens-rerecording Sega Genesis / Mega Drive
.vbm VBA-rerecording Game Boy / GBC / GBA
.m64 Mupen64 N64
.smv Snes9x-rerecording SNES
.pxm PCSX-rerecording PSX
.pjm PSXjin (text body) PSX
.dtm Dolphin GameCube
.lmp Doom (vanilla 1.9) DOS / PC

Every parser produces the same in-memory shape: a replayr_movie S3 object with a (n_frames, n_players, n_buttons) logical input array indexed against a single 40-slot universal-button layout, plus the file’s header metadata and a per-frame commands vector.

replayr universal-button layout

Slots 1–30 cover the gamepad family (d-pad, Start/Select/Mode, six face buttons, two shoulders, two triggers, four C-buttons, and the eight stick directions). Slots 31–40 cover the Intellivision / ColecoVision numeric keypad. INTV’s Enter / Clear and Coleco’s Star / Pound fold into Start (slot 5) and Select (slot 6) — they’re pressed once at boot, not as gameplay verbs, so they share semantics with console Start/Select rather than getting their own slots.

Quick start 

library(replayr)

# Use one of the bundled samples.
fp <- system.file("extdata", "sample.fm2", package = "replayr")
mv <- read_movie(fp)
mv
#> <replayr_movie [fm2] frames=3600 players=2 buttons=8 source=sample.fm2>

n_frames(mv)            # frame count
press_counts(mv)        # named vector of per-button hold counts
p1 <- player(mv, 1L)    # logical matrix (frames x buttons)

system.file("extdata", package = "replayr") lists every bundled sample. To parse your own movie file, just pass the path:

mv <- read_movie("/path/to/your/movie.bk2")

Universal button layout

The 40-slot universal-button alphabet is documented in ?universal_buttons. Slots 1..8 are NES-shaped (R, L, D, U, Start, Select, B, A); higher slots cover SNES face/shoulder buttons, the N64 C-buttons, an 8-direction quantisation of any analog stick, and PSX- specific L2/R2. n_buttons(mv) tells you how many slots a particular movie actually uses (8 NES, 12 SNES, 15 Genesis, 28 N64/GameCube, 30 PSX).

Install

From a local source tree:

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install("path/to/replayr")

Test 

devtools::test("path/to/replayr")

The test suite is self-contained: twelve generated one-minute samples exercise every supported reader. They contain only synthetic controller input and no third-party movie data. Set REPLAYR_FIXTURE_DIR to a separately obtained local corpus if you want to run optional compatibility tests as well; corpus files are never bundled with replayr.

License

replayr is licensed under the GNU General Public License version 2 or later. Six of the twelve format readers were developed with reference to the upstream emulator’s source tree (named in those files’ headers); those upstreams are themselves GPL-2+, so the package as a whole is GPL.

Acknowledgements

The format-specific readers build on documentation and reference implementations from the speedrunning / TAS community. We are grateful to the authors of these projects for keeping their formats open enough to be re-implemented:

  • Dolphin Emulator Project – the .dtm GameCube movie format reader (R/read_dtm.R) was developed with reference to Source/Core/Core/Movie.cpp.
  • id Software’s Doom source – the .lmp demo format reader (R/read_lmp.R) was developed with reference to linuxdoom-1.10/g_game.c and the DoomWiki demo specification.
  • PSXjin – the .pjm reader was developed with reference to the PSXjin source tree.
  • PCSX-rerecording – the .pxm reader follows the PCSX-rr format and its documented controller-record layout.
  • lsnes – the .lsmv movie format reader was developed with reference to the lsnes source tree.
  • VBA-rerecording – the .vbm movie format reader was developed with reference to movie.h.
  • TASVideos – the EmulatorResources wiki provides community-authored format documentation. Every reader cites at least one TASVideos page.
  • FCEUX – the .fm2 format spec is the canonical reference for the FCEUX movie format.

Per-file attribution comments name the specific upstream references for each derivative reader. The full provenance manifest is in inst/COPYRIGHTS.

The .fm2, .bk2, .fcm, .gmv, .m64, and .smv readers were written from public format specifications and to our knowledge do not draw on any GPL emulator source, but they are still covered by the package’s GPL (>= 2) license.
